import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/test_4.csv"
]

# List to hold dataframes
dfs = []

# Load each source CSV into a dataframe
# All source tables have the exact same schema as the target:
# ['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']
# So we can union (concat) them directly.
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    # Ensure columns are exactly as target schema and in order
    df = df[['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']]
    dfs.append(df)

# Concatenate all source dataframes (union)
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# The target schema columns are all strings, so convert all columns to string type
for col in ['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']:
    combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].astype(str)

# The target examples show that the 'Winner' column contains "YES" or presumably "NO"
# We keep it as is, no transformation needed.

# Write the combined dataframe to the target CSV path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_66/target_multisource_cot.csv"
combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
